Genericity comes from per-tenant config plus pluggable per-language analysers (Go now via go/ast, others later through the same bundle contract — the way deploy already has github-now / other-adapters-later). Build each trial piece in this shape so what a trial teaches (e.g. the wiring-include) lands as a feature of the action that ships, not as throwaway scaffolding.
- **Two layers, both multi-agent — keep them distinct.** The website-builder (the chassis: adoption, planner, content, research, imagery, rerender, deploy) is the subject the tool helps develop, and a product in its own right. The context tool is the development layer that assembles task context and verifies changes to that builder (and, generically, to any codebase). The builder builds sites; the tool builds reliable changes to the builder. Neither replaces the other; focusing on the tool hasn't dropped the builder — it sits one layer down.
- **The remaining gaps are all "find", not "include".** The tool can include any code (`-scope`) or any doc (`-doc`), but it can't yet *find* the relevant one for a task automatically. Target-resolution (which code), matched-standards retrieval (which guidelines), and the wiring-include (the code a call graph can't reach) are the same missing capability from different sides — selection/retrieval, not inclusion. Concretely for documentation: the analyser reads code only; guidelines enter via the always-on constitution plus manual `-doc`; auto-selecting the relevant guideline is the deferred standards/docs contributor — a named-but-hand-filled slot in the bundle.
- **"Different angles" are all contributors; "checkers" are a separate concept.** The build's different angles are two kinds of *contributor*: context contributors each assemble one slice of the bundle (code, data, runtime, standards), and build-time review contributors each review the proposed change from one angle (reuse, duplication, liability, morality, correctness), raising a concern that revises the change or gates via HITL. Separate containers keep each angle's logs and responsibility distinct. **Checkers are not these:** in the web tool a checker is an improvement-loop agent that continuously monitors *deployed* sites against the plan/spec (the existing `check_*.go` family), usually with a fixer — it runs post-deployment, on a loop, in the builder/operate layer, not in the build path. Whether the initial builds reuse some of the same checks is unconfirmed and is to be investigated separately. (The website-builder layer also has its own context-angle agents — research, content, design, imagery — same pattern, lower layer.)
- **A morality review is a distinct angle from liability, and must apply a configured standard, not a baked-in view.** Liability asks "will this get us sued or fined"; morality asks "is this right" — they overlap but some legal things are still wrong. The tool must not hard-code one moral view: the morality review (a build-time contributor) applies a *layered, configured* standard held in the active-config — a base framework the operator chooses (for marketing sites, advertising/consumer-protection standards like the UK ASA/CAP code and CMA guidance, plus recognised AI-ethics frameworks for the generation angle), the operator's own judgement on top with priority, and later jurisdiction/government guidance and a current-focus overlay as higher-priority dated sources. It runs at two altitudes (per-output, and a vertical-level gate at intake on the domain/objective), and because moral calls are contested it routes hard cases to a human (HITL) rather than auto-resolving. The tool applies the configured standard and flags; it is not the moral authority.
- **A trial finding can land as a tool feature, as intended.** The first adoption run showed the call graph misses wiring/registration files (`registry.go`); that taught the rule, and the rule shipped as the assembler's `-include` flag (force-include named wiring/shared files regardless of the call graph). The trial's output was throwaway; the capability it specified is now in the tool — the "build trial pieces so they graduate" principle, demonstrated.
- **First real assembler run, on the actual adoption code, confirmed the thesis and the limits.** Scoped to the two decisive functions (`LoadPageSectionsFromSpecAction`, `PlanSectionsAction`) with `-include registry.go`, it produced a ~30 KB bundle against the script's ~1.7 MB (≈57×), and the call graph surfaced exactly the readiness/section-resolution helpers that matter (`planSection`, `createDeferredItems`, `loadComponentSchemas`, `resolveSectionComponent`, …) — neighbourhood adequacy confirmed for this task, with the `registry.go` wiring now present via `-include`. Two honest caveats: the neighbourhood is only as complete as the analysed tree (six files here, so it's a floor — a full-tree run would also pull callees living in other files), and the genuinely-missing contributor for a debug task is runtime evidence (the run trace/errors the script's live-capture block carried but the assembler still stubs).
- **Runtime evidence is built, by extending dbcontext rather than adding a tool.** `dbcontext -runtime-site <domain>` (optionally `-runtime-page`) pulls recent `agent_error_log` rows and the `site_work_items` lifecycle and renders a "Runtime evidence" block; the assembler's `-runtime <file>` slots it into that section. It reused dbcontext's psql/CSV/table machinery (reuse before recreate). On the skinner-box data the lifecycle it pulls *is* the diagnosis — the timed-out original item and the empty-but-`complete` retry. The two tables it queries (`agent_error_log`, `site_work_items`) are the ones whose schema is confirmed; the run-state table (`orchestration_states`) is left for `-rows` until its schema is verified.
- **Target resolution has a deterministic baseline before any embeddings — and it shows its own recall gap.** `resolve_targets.go` scores symbols against the task by name/path/doc word-overlap and proposes the `-scope` set (plus wiring `-include`s by detecting registry-like files). On the skinner-box task it ranked `PlanSectionsAction` first and surfaced the whole section-planning cluster and `registry.go` — but it ranked `LoadPageSectionsFromSpecAction` (also decisive, name echoing "load/spec" not the task's "plan/ready/count") below the cut. That miss is the exact recall gap embeddings fill, and the baseline says so itself. Sequencing held: lexical first (cheap, no infra, and useful), embeddings later when there's a ground-truth set to prove they beat it.
- **Omitting bodies shifts the burden of completeness onto the assembler — the complement is giving the model a retrieval tool, not abandoning curation.** Signatures-not-bodies buys focus and token-efficiency but removes the model's ability to grep the codebase itself; if the bundle omits a body it needs, it's stuck, and the onus is on us to have included the right files. The fix isn't to dump more — it's an on-demand search/read tool the model can call to fetch what the seed bundle lacks (the index, call graph, body-by-line-range, `dbcontext`, and the lexical resolver are already its backends). This is how capable coding agents work: a small seed plus tools to pull the rest. Not a bad idea — a good one — with caveats: it complements curation rather than replacing it (a good seed means fewer fetches); the same size discipline applies to fetched results (probe, signatures first, bodies only when needed) or context rot returns; it should offer both lexical and semantic search (so it's the same investment as the embedding layer, seen from the agent's side); read-only and tenant-scoped; and record what was fetched (provenance). It also shifts the shape from "assemble-and-paste a bundle" to "assemble a seed and serve tools" — which is exactly the agentic/workflow form the tool is heading toward, so it's a direction to take when the tool becomes agentic, not a contradiction of the bundle approach.
- **Stay foundation-model-agnostic; the embedder (and any model call) sits behind an interface, and we have our own models to serve it.** The platform has a small Ollama CPU model (the `ollama-adapter` / `ollama-eval` pods) for cheap, local embedding and inference, and Thunder GPU (the finetuning-flywheel project) for heavy/bulk work. So the model-dependent layers can use a real self-hosted model (e.g. `nomic-embed-text` via Ollama) rather than a stand-in or an external API — and because it's behind an `Embedder` interface, the model stays swappable. Model-agnosticism is a hard constraint, not a preference: don't couple the tool to any one provider's mechanisms.
- **The embedding layer is built (`embed.go`) — mechanism verified, real recall pending a model run.** `embed build` indexes the analyser's symbols (name + kind + signature + doc + path, embedded then L2-normalised) and `embed query` returns cosine top-k for a task; two embedders — an Ollama client (POST `{model,input[]}` to `/api/embed`) and an offline token-hashing stand-in. Tested here with the stand-in (proves index→cosine→rank→suggested-scope) and against a stub HTTP server (proves the Ollama request/response handling, batched build + single-text query). The stand-in is *not* semantic, so the recall gain over the lexical baseline is only demonstrable by running `query -ollama` against the real model, and only *measurable* once a ground-truth task→files set exists. Index and query must use the same embedder (same vector space). Next: merge the lexical and semantic candidate sets into one `-scope` proposal.
- **PARKED for a dedicated discussion: provider-native tool use vs a model-agnostic second round-trip.** The agentic search-tool direction would normally use the model's native tool-calling, but that is provider-specific and breaks model-agnosticism. The model-agnostic alternative: the model states what it needs in its text/JSON output, the orchestrator fulfils it via our tools, and feeds it back on the next API turn — no provider tool-calling. Attractive because it keeps agnosticism and full control over what's fetched (so the size discipline still applies); the tradeoffs are added latency (full round-trips vs streamed tool calls) and needing the model to emit a reliably-parseable need-spec. Flagged, not resolved — to compare properly when the tool goes agentic.
- **The merge and the measurement harness are built — and the measurement immediately corrected an assertion.** `fuse.go` combines candidate lists by reciprocal-rank fusion (rank-based, so the lexical integer scores and semantic cosine scores need no common scale); `eval_targets.go` scores any candidate list against `groundtruth_targets.json` (recall@N, MRR, hits/misses), with suffix-tolerant path matching so one ground-truth file works for both a flat dir and the full tree. Running the whole chain on the adoption analysis showed three things worth keeping: (1) the lexical resolver actually surfaces *both* decisive symbols within top-12 (`PlanSectionsAction` #1, `LoadPageSectionsFromSpecAction` #12) — so my earlier "it misses it" was too strong; it gets it but borderline, which is the real thing the semantic layer should improve (rank it robustly, not at the cut). (2) The offline stand-in is non-semantic noise (recall 0/2), confirming it is only good for plumbing, never for judging quality. (3) **Fusing a strong list with a weak one degrades the result** (fused recall 0/2): plain RRF rewards agreement, so a decisive item only one list ranks high gets diluted. The consequence: the merge cannot be validated with the stand-in — it needs the real Ollama list, and if one list dominates we should weight the fusion rather than use plain RRF. This is the "measure rather than assert" principle paying for itself on the first run.
- **The toolset is now one module with the contracts defined once, not seven files re-declaring them.** The duplicate names (`analysis` ×3, `funcDef`/`typeDef` clashing between analyser and assembler, `candFile` ×2) were the visible symptom; the real issue was the same two contracts — the analyser's output shape and the ranked-candidate shape — hand-redefined in every consumer. Fix: a `contextkit` module with `internal/analysis` and `internal/candidates` holding each contract once, and each tool as its own `cmd/<name>` command (which also dissolves the `main`/`funcDef`/`typeDef` clashes, since each command is a separate package). Consumers reference the shared types by qualified name (`analysis.FuncDef`, `candidates.Candidate`) — no per-tool aliases, one unambiguous source. `dbcontext` shares neither contract, so it imports neither. When these graduate into the chassis, the same two packages move under the chassis module path; nothing else changes. Run shifts from `go run x.go` to `go run ./cmd/x` / `go build ./...`. (An intermediate version used local type aliases to keep the diffs tiny; the qualified-name form was chosen as the final state for a single, explicit reference to each contract.)
- **The target shape in the chassis is an index/build split, recorded in its own living plan (`PLAN_workflows_and_actions_migration.md`) — discussion-first, unknowns before code.** When `contextkit` moves into the chassis: a durable **indexing** workflow (commit-triggered, SHA-keyed: code structure + embeddings) feeds a per-task **build** workflow (resolve targets → optional HITL scope confirm → gather context slices → assemble → generate → review → emit). The action-vs-agent rule: something is an **agent** when it should be a separately-logged orchestrator that can recurse or gate at HITL (the context contributors and the build-time review contributors), and an **action** when a step-level log entry over pure compute is enough (`resolve_targets` with lexical+semantic+fusion folded in, `assemble_bundle`). No subworkflows in SQL — separable concerns are spawned sub-agents replying on the parent topic. Reuse the chassis DB layer, the ollama-adapter, the registry, the spawn/topic wiring, the generation adapter, and artifact upload rather than the thin-slice stand-ins; `eval_targets` stays offline as the measurement harness. The plan deliberately front-loads the doubts — the workflow-definition and orchestration schema are the gate (we've only inferred them from step names), and the parked on-demand-context-vs-assemble-then-send fork has to be settled because it decides whether gathering is a fixed sequence or a loop. Nothing is built; the next move is confirming the live-system schema/APIs, not writing workflows.
- **The workflow/agent model is now grounded in the guide docs (001/002), and it corrected the migration plan.** Workflows are declarative JSON in `agent_definitions.default_config` (templates_db); steps are `{action, config, next_step, output_field}`; there's a generic action library to reuse before writing Go (`query_database`, `spawn_agent`, `call_agent`, `loop`, `conditional`, `rag_lookup`, the work-item lifecycle). Two corrections to what I'd proposed: the chassis deliberately **groups** LLM-assisted checks into group-agents by shared context (one context load, one call per group) rather than making each its own agent — so the build-time reviews are a group agent, not four separate agents — with a **promotion pattern** to spawn a sub-agent only when one check needs independence; and much of "gather/generate" maps to existing generic actions, so there are fewer new Go actions than first listed. The most important reuse check is `rag_lookup`: a retrieval action already exists and may overlap with `embed`/`resolve_targets`, so confirm-and-reuse before building a parallel index. The remaining genuine unknowns shrank to the run-trace tables (for runtime evidence) and whether a HITL pause/resume step exists. Lesson reinforced: read the guides before proposing structure — half my "open questions" were already answered there.
- **Real `agent_definitions` rows + the action code made "what is an agent" concrete, and produced two decisions.** An agent is a DB row whose `default_config.workflow` is a step graph; the Go code holds *actions* (`SpawnAgentAction`, `CallAgentAction`, `ExecuteLLMPromptAction`), never agents — which is why it isn't obvious from a code read. `spawn_agent`+`call_agent` are a pair (spawn creates the Job and wires the child's parent-responses topic; call sends the work), and an agent's description can contradict its config (`build-dispatch-loop` claims "no loops or sub_workflows" but its config has a `loop`+`sub_workflow`) — folded into debug guide §6.0. Decisions: (1) the build's **gather phase is a loop**, not a fixed sequence — tasks get long, and the `loop` action + existing `call_agent`-substep loops + `rag_lookup` are precedent; the model-agnostic "ask for more" is still the parked second-round-trip, now scoped to the loop with a budget/termination to define. (2) **CPU Ollama must be feasibility-checked early** on speed (embed the whole chassis; per-query latency) and quality (beat the lexical baseline on the ground-truth set) before the embedding layer leans on it — Thunder GPU or a different model if it falls short, and reuse `rag_lookup`'s embedder if it already has a workable one.

## DB discipline

- **Snapshot before any `agent_definitions` change; check `\df` for a helper before hand-writing SQL.** The DB carries helper functions — `snapshot_agent(p_agent_type)` and `snapshot_agent(p_agent_type, p_reason)` (both return uuid), with `revert_agent` to roll back. Run a snapshot before *any* change to `agent_definitions` (config patch, migration, manual edit); it's cheap insurance against the patch-contamination / failed-revert footguns. More generally, reuse-before-recreate applies at the DB layer too: before writing raw SQL for something routine, run `\df` and see whether a function already does it. Recorded in debug guide §0 (item 24) and §6.2. **To do (long-term):** capture the full live `\df` output into §6.2 — it currently holds only the confirmed helpers as a scaffold; we should keep a real inventory in the docs so helpers are discoverable rather than re-derived each time.
- **pgvector appears installed.** The same `\df` snippet listed `sparsevec` (a pgvector artefact), so pgvector is likely present — confirm with `\dx`. If so, embedding storage should use pgvector columns + similarity operators from the start rather than in-Go cosine, which also resolves the at-scale storage question (migration plan B4/B4a).
- **DB capabilities (`\dx`/`\df`) are captured *context*, not memory — and the capture point is `dbcontext`, not the analyser.** Reuse-before-recreate at the DB layer only works if generation can *see* what exists: installed extensions (pgvector available) and helper functions (reuse `snapshot_agent`, don't hand-roll a backup table — the migration-110 footgun). So the bundle should carry `\dx`+`\df` for DB-touching tasks. Built in the harness: `dbcontext -capabilities` runs both (same psql path it already uses for `\d`), and the assembler gained a `-dbfacts` **Database capabilities** section that includes the capture, with a reuse nudge when absent. Clear division: the **analyser is code only** (Go-AST, language-agnostic contract); **DB facts live in `dbcontext` + the assembler section** — don't conflate them. The durable step (recorded as plan B2a): fold the capture into the indexing workflow on a *migration cadence* (these change on migrations, not every commit) so the bundle always carries current capabilities without anyone remembering a flag; gate by task type for size. Debug-guide §6.2 is the human-readable twin.
- **The chassis already has the embedding/retrieval layer I was prototyping — reuse it, don't parallel it.** `rag_actions.go` shows `rag_index`/`rag_lookup` running `nomic-embed-text` via the `ollama-adapter` (with the asymmetric `search_document:`/`search_query:` nomic prefixes) into a **pgvector** store (`knowledge_base`, cosine `<=>`, idempotent dedup on `content_hash`), with a trigram fallback. So pgvector is confirmed in use (closes the storage question), and `embed`/`fuse`/`resolve_targets`/`eval_targets` are repositioned as the lexical layer + fusion + offline measurement, not a parallel vector store. The one genuine misfit for code: `rag_index`'s character chunker fragments functions — code must be chunked at **symbol boundaries**, which the analyser already gives. So contextkit indexing = analyser symbols → nomic prefix → the *same* embedder → a `knowledge_base`-shaped store. Made `embed` faithful (added the nomic prefixes mirroring `applyNomicPrefix`) so the CPU-Ollama feasibility run measures nomic the way the chassis actually uses it. The two checks merge: running feasibility through the analyser-symbol path also proves the embedder reuse works for code. One input still needed to finalise: `\d knowledge_base` (columns, vector dim, ANN index).
- **The embedding stack is confirmed end-to-end and reusable — this closes the storage/embedder questions and narrows feasibility to one real risk.** Ground truth from `\d knowledge_base` (clients_db) + `aiservice/interface.go` + `ollama.go`: a model-agnostic embedder seam already exists (`AIService.GenerateEmbedding`, `OllamaClient`, `nomic-embed-text`; the caller applies the nomic `search_document:`/`search_query:` prefix, which `embed.go`'s `nomicPrefix` mirrors), and the store is pgvector `knowledge_base.embedding vector(768)` with an **IVFFlat cosine** ANN index AND a **gin_trgm** index on `content` in the same table — i.e. the chassis already does the lexical+semantic hybrid I built, and the fusion can run in SQL (so the in-Go `fuse` may not graduate). Consequences: reuse the embedder + pgvector + the hybrid pattern + the dedup (`unique(collection, content_hash)`); code symbols get a **sibling table** mirroring that shape (not a KB collection — different columns and lifecycle), preferring **HNSW** over IVFFlat because the code index updates incrementally per commit (IVFFlat centroids go stale and need REINDEX as rows churn). `contextkit`'s `embed`/`resolve_targets`/`fuse`/`eval_targets` are confirmed as the offline lexical-prototyping + measurement layer with a clean graduation path (swap my embedder for `AIService.GenerateEmbedding`, swap in-memory cosine for the pgvector table). The one remaining embedding risk is **code-domain quality** — nomic is prose-trained, so measure code recall with `eval_targets` against the real adapter; per-query latency is de-risked by the ANN index, and "is it wired" is answered (the model serves the KB; `ollama-eval` 47d uptime). Endpoint nuance: `GenerateEmbedding` uses `/api/embeddings` (single text); my stand-in used `/api/embed` (batch) — reuse `AIService`, batch via a loop.
- **The code index store is now a concrete artifact: a `code_symbols` sibling table (DDL drafted), reusing the KB shape, keyed for code.** Decisions realised: sibling table (not a `knowledge_base` collection — different columns/lifecycle); identity `unique(repo, path, symbol)` with `content_hash` to skip re-embedding unchanged symbols; SHA-versioned via `commit_sha`; HNSW primary (incremental-friendly) with IVFFlat fallback. Two deliberate, flagged departures from the usual conventions, because this is a rebuildable cache not a system-of-record entity: no `version`/`previous_version_id` (versioned by commit), and no `deleted_at` (stale symbols are pruned/hard-deleted, not soft-deleted). The migration honours the §6.1 footgun (plain `CREATE TABLE`, not `IF NOT EXISTS`, so a pre-existing table errors) and carries the parameterised retrieval/upsert/prune queries — including the hybrid RRF done in SQL, which is what lets the in-Go `fuse` retire. Still gated on `\dx` (HNSW needs pgvector >= 0.5.0) and a `\dt` reuse check before apply.
- **Pre-apply gates passed; `code_symbols` is clear to apply on `clients_db`.** `\dt` found no existing code/symbol table; `\dx` shows pgvector **0.8.0** with HNSW (so the primary HNSW index stands, no IVFFlat fallback), pg_trgm 1.6, and pgcrypto for `gen_random_uuid()`. Storage questions (A5/B4) fully closed. The one open embedding question is now B4a — whether nomic retrieves code well enough to beat the trigram baseline — which the table plus the offline harness (`eval_targets` against the real adapter, nomic prefix applied) are set up to answer. Discipline that paid off: gating the apply on `\dt` (reuse) + `\dx` (HNSW availability) rather than assuming, and using plain `CREATE TABLE` so a pre-existing table would have surfaced.
- **Decided: text-embedding and code-embedding are separate responsibilities — share the mechanism, separate the policy.** Shared (don't duplicate): the `AIService` embedder seam (model-agnostic, per-agent `ai_service` config), provider impls, pgvector, the semantic+trigram hybrid. Separate per domain so each improves independently: the model (prose vs code-specific — the main lever and the answer to B4a's domain shift), the vector dimension (follows the model; isolated by separate tables), preprocessing (nomic prefixes vs a code model's), retrieval tuning (HNSW vs IVFFlat, lexical-heavier hybrid for code), the row definition (symbol vs prose chunk), and evaluation (code vs text ground-truth). The sibling table started this; the `embedding_model` column lets one domain be re-embedded after a model upgrade without touching the other. Chassis form: separate indexer agents (knowledge over `knowledge_base`, code over `code_symbols`), each with its own `ai_service`. Open: parameterise `rag_lookup` by table+model+weights vs a sibling code-retrieval action (lean sibling if ranking diverges). Caution: separation only pays if the shared mechanism stays shared — policy separate, plumbing shared. (`code_symbols` applied cleanly this turn.)
- **Harness embedder realigned to the chassis contract so the B4a measurement is faithful and turnkey.** `embed.go`'s Ollama embedder now does single-call `/api/embeddings` `{model,prompt}` (was batch `/api/embed` `{model,input[]}`), matching `ollama.go` and the `AIService.GenerateEmbedding` graduation seam exactly — same model, same `search_document:`/`search_query:` prefixes as `rag_*`. Why: it predicts production behaviour, hits the endpoint the chassis provably serves (de-risks the run against the adapter), and measures realistic single-call indexing latency (the SPEED half of B4a). Trade-off: single-call is slower for bulk than batch — but that slowness *is* the speed signal; batch `/api/embed` is a later optimisation only if the adapter exposes it. Only `ollamaEmbedder` changed; no variable names elsewhere. Built + vetted + smoke-tested against a fake `/api/embeddings` server; tarball refreshed. The runbook now carries the full measurement procedure (lexical baseline vs semantic-against-real-adapter vs fused, the decision rule, and the "which model for code" repeat with `-model`). The measurement remains the user's to run (needs the chassis repo + live adapter); it is the one open embedding risk and the gate before committing the code-indexing path to a model.
- **Code-indexer reuse target grounded from `rag_actions.go` — reuse the mechanism, differ on what's code-specific.** The chassis already has `rag_index` (chunk→embed→store in `knowledge_base`) and `rag_lookup` (embed→vector search→trigram fallback). Reuse as-is (same `actions` package, direct calls): `createRAGEmbeddingClient`, `applyNomicPrefix`, `pgvectorString`, and the pattern (sha256 content_hash dedup; embedding non-fatal so trigram still works; `ON CONFLICT`). Differ: input is analyser symbols not a blob and is NOT chunked (`rag_index`'s `chunkContent` breaks Go mid-function — the prose chunker A5 flagged); target is `code_symbols`; conflict is identity upsert `(repo,path,symbol) DO UPDATE WHERE content_hash IS DISTINCT` not content `DO NOTHING` (KB is content-keyed, code is identity-keyed); retrieval is its own query because `vectorSearchKB`/`trigramSearchKB` bake in KB's table+columns. So build a thin `index_code_symbols` + a `lookup_code_symbols` (mirrors rag_lookup) reusing the helpers; the indexer agent is a one-step-each orchestrator (analyser → index → prune), needing the analyser-as-library. Resolved the parked B4b retrieval sub-decision → sibling action, not a parameterised rag_lookup. Separately: **docs reuse the existing rag path as-is** (prose → a `knowledge_base` collection like `standards`, retrieved by `rag_lookup`) — flat files stay the source of truth, the DB copy is a derived retrieval index; much lighter than code, keep it a distinct workstream. Constraint: chassis Go compiles in the user's env (module `github.com/gqls/agentchassis/...`), not in-container — these actions get drafted for review, then built/deployed via their GitHub Actions → Backblaze pipeline.
- **Production is in-cluster; the contextkit harness is a prototyping/measurement scaffold (framing corrected).** Parsing, indexing, retrieval, and context assembly are in-cluster chassis capabilities — no desktop dependency. The harness binaries proved the approach and measure recall (a dev/tuning activity for the flywheel); their production-relevant parts graduate in-cluster (analyser → adapter; embed → `index_code_symbols`; hybrid → SQL over `code_symbols`; assembler → a build action), leaving `eval_targets` + ground truth as the measurement tool. My earlier "analyses locally and offline" was imprecise: the Go walk is a library because it's the parsing *primitive the in-cluster adapter wraps*, not because anything is desktop-bound.
- **Decided: build the polyglot analyser adapter NOW.** Reason (the right test): the JS tools already exist and need code-symbol indexing/provenance — tech debt, not a foreseeable-future plan, so build polyglot-ready once. Three layers, decision applied: (1) Go AST walk = a **library** (`analysis.Analyse`), extracted from `cmd/analyser`, still needed because it runs *inside* the adapter (a polyglot adapter imports it for Go, doesn't replace it); (2) an **`Analyser` seam** the code-indexer depends on (interface `Analyse(repo, ref, language) → Output`), mirroring how callers depend on `AIService` not `OllamaClient`; (3) the **adapter = a service**, fronting per-language parsers like the ollama-adapter fronts models, taking `(repo, ref, language)` and returning symbols over HTTP. The seam means `index_code_symbols` can be drafted against the interface now, independent of the adapter build.
- **JS's three needs are distinct — keep the adapter's scope precise.** Code-symbol *indexing* needs a JS parser → the adapter (JS drop-in). *Documentation* is prose → the language-agnostic `rag_index` path, no parser. *Provenance* is recorded by `code_symbols` (commit_sha, path, symbol) for any language. Separately and far-future (NOT an analyser concern): the *performance* of the end-user quant tools the chassis builds (TCP tricks, faster languages) is product code in the generated sites, handled when those tools are built — the analyser only parses those languages well enough to index them.
- **Parsing input = git checkout in-cluster, not raw files in B2/Postgres.** The repo is the editable source of truth; the checkout is ephemeral; Postgres holds only the derived index (symbols/chunks + embeddings + searchable content); B2 is for built deliverables. Flow: checkout repo@SHA into a container workspace → parse/read → derived index to Postgres (`code_symbols`; a `knowledge_base` collection for docs) → discard checkout. The adapter owns the checkout for code (clones repo@ref, parses, returns symbols); docs are read from a checkout and fed to `rag_index`. Precondition: the docs must live in a git repo — if they're loose files (desktop/chat project), step one is putting them in git; "flat files as source of truth" = "files in a versioned repo", not on a machine. Do NOT store raw docs in Postgres (that's the index) or lean on B2 for the editable source (artifacts only). Access choice to settle: cluster clones from GitHub (a read token/deploy key as a k8s secret) or fetches a B2 source snapshot from the existing pipeline — cloning is the simpler default, B2-snapshot avoids cluster git creds.
- **Adapter build grounded in the real git/thunder adapters — and the transport was Kafka, not HTTP (correction).** Custom adapters (git, thunder) are Kafka workers: consume `AdapterRequest{Headers, Body{Action, Data}}` from a requests topic, dispatch by action, reply with a `ResponseMessage{Headers, Body{Success, Data, Error}}` on the caller's `responses_topic` (shapes in `platform/models`; `ToKafkaHeaders()` flattens). Only the *stock* ollama-adapter is HTTP — which is why my earlier "analyser adapter = HTTP service" was wrong. "Output messages pass validation" = this ResponseMessage contract. Dispatcher pattern from thunder/adapter.go (kafka consumer+producer, `Run` loop, `handleMessage` → dispatch → reply); handler shape from thunder action handlers (`NewXAction(deps)` + `Execute(ctx, req)`, stateless/idempotent).
- **Adapter progress this turn:** extracted + compiled the layer-1 `analysis.Analyse(root)` (contextkit `internal/analysis/analyse.go`; CLI now thin) — moves to the chassis as `internal/analysis`. Drafted (chassis, for their build) `github_source.go` (read-only **tarball** fetch — one request, no git binary, recovers `commit_sha` from the archive top-dir, traversal-guarded) and `analyse_action.go` (validate → fetch → Analyse → result; Go-only, JS parser drop-in behind the same action). Next: dispatcher + manifest (mirror thunder), then the `index_code_symbols` consumer.
- **Security/repo-access decided direction:** least-privilege, per-adapter — the analyser gets a fine-grained, **repo-scoped, read-only** GitHub token (k8s Secret, mounted only on its pod); the git adapter keeps its separate **write** credential. Not broad cluster access, not one shared token. Reuse the git adapter's GitHub-API client pattern; fetch via tarball. Harden with rotation, encrypted secrets, network policy; the indexed code stays in the existing in-cluster Postgres trust boundary. No-static-secret variant: a GitHub App installation token (short-lived, auto-rotating).
- **JS tools documentation flagged as its own focus (`FOCUS_js_tools_documentation.md`).** The existing JS tools need prose docs + provenance and have neither; only the site/plan spec they were built from exists (a seed, not documentation). Two mechanisms: prose docs → the language-agnostic `rag_index`/`knowledge_base` path (no parser); code-symbol provenance → the analyser adapter's JS parser drop-in (records via `code_symbols`). Docs must live in git to be indexable. Tech debt (the tools exist now), not a future plan.
- **Import-reuse confirmed for the message envelope (user was right).** Canonical types are in `platform/orchestration/types` (context.go): RequestMessage/RequestHeaders (Action + ResponsesTopic on the HEADERS), ResponseMessage/ResponseHeaders/ResponseBody{Success,Body,Error}/ErrorInfo, AgentIdentity, and the helpers `FromRequestHeaders(headers)→*ExecutionContext` + `(ec)ToResponseHeaders()→ResponseHeaders`. The adapter IMPORTS these and builds responses via FromRequestHeaders→set status/sender→ToResponseHeaders, so the platform constructs the envelope (best guarantee of passing validation). git mirrored the types locally = the duplication to avoid. Cyclic-import handling here (interfaces.go: MessageTracer local "to avoid cyclic import") is for behavioral interfaces, not data types — importing the data types is clean.
- **Adapter naming settled: `analyser`** (`system.adapter.analyser.requests`, group `analyser.adapter.group`). Convention = name for the capability fronted (thunder/git/ollama → analyser fronts parsers). Product names (contextkit/contexttool/doctool) name the consumer; renamable.
- **Dispatcher built (`adapter.go`, chassis draft).** Mirrors thunder/adapter.go (kafka consumer+producer, NewAdapter with env topic/group + read-only GitHubSource, Run fetch-loop + small /health,/ready server, handleMessage). Reuses orchestration/types for the contract + ToResponseHeaders. Manifest built (`analyser-adapter.yaml`): Deployment + read-only repo-scoped Secret `analyser-github-read` + health probes. Reconcile only: (1) kafka pkg path + NewConsumer/NewProducer/FetchMessage/Produce/CommitMessages signatures from thunder; (2) the ExecutionContext fields ToResponseHeaders needs (Sender/Status/IsComplete/IsError) + AgentIdentity field names.
- **Analyser adapter now complete as drafts** (fetcher + handler + dispatcher + manifest + the compiled analysis library). Next: consumer side — index_code_symbols + lookup_code_symbols + the indexer agent (call analyser adapter → upsert code_symbols → prune), then end-to-end (index chassis → B4a → assemble).
- **Adapter Response Envelope Contract (doc 003) — the silent-timeout trap, and my draft had it.** An adapter reply must set, in the KAFKA MESSAGE HEADERS: message_type=response, **request_id = the incoming request_id reused verbatim** (the router matches awaited_requests on this), fresh message_id, in_response_to_request_id, orchestration_id, correlation_id, status, sender_agent_type, in_response_to_step_id/name; and be sent via **ProduceWithValidation** (not Produce). Body headers unmarshal into types.ResponseHeaders where is_complete/is_error are real bool — so the body MUST use a typed struct (ToResponseHeaders), never map[string]string string-bools. Get any of these wrong and the reply routes to process-as-work and the awaited row times out with no error logged (real multi-day thunder fault). Reference adapters: webscrape (map builder) + git (typed ResponseHeaders + ToKafkaHeaders).
- **Correction: import-reuse alone is insufficient for the adapter response envelope.** Canonical types.ResponseHeaders has NO request_id/message_id field and NO ToKafkaHeaders method (verified in context.go). So: body reuses the canonical type (real bools via ToResponseHeaders); the adapter ADDS a local Kafka-header builder (git's ToKafkaHeaders analog) + ProduceWithValidation. That's why git mirrored locally — not arbitrary duplication. Fixed adapter.go accordingly.
- **Consumer side scoping (per 001/003):** index_code_symbols + lookup_code_symbols are ACTIONS (mirror rag_index/rag_lookup; platform/orchestration/actions/code_symbols_actions.go; ActionInputSpec+ExtractActionInputs; parameterised SQL; reuse rag embedding helpers). code-indexer is an AGENT (agent_definitions row, category integrator) — orchestrator: request_analysis (call analyser adapter) → index → complete. Field names prefixed (repo, not site_id/domain) to dodge ExtractActionInputs nested-source collisions (current_page/rerender_pages/site_record/input_data).
- **To build the consumer side right first time, need 4 source files** (same discipline as the user sending the kafka package for the dispatcher): rag_actions.go (reuse exact helpers + signatures), an adapter-calling action (webscrape/git's chassis-side caller, for the analyser request-reply), action_registry.go (registration), one sample agent_definitions row (workflow + contracts + docker_image/tag + category). Building blind risks 001's resolveRAGFieldPath / universal-topic-fallback anti-patterns.
- **ProduceWithValidation signature (verified, webscrape_actions.go):** `ProduceWithValidation(ctx, topic string, headers map[string]string, key []byte, value []byte) error` — headers BEFORE key. My adapter had key/value/headers order; fixed.
- **Adapter-call pattern (verified, WebscrapeAction):** an action that calls a fixed-topic adapter builds JSON `{headers, body}`, derives the responses topic from `ExecutionContext.ResponsesTopic` (fallbacks: env RESPONSES_TOPIC, then `system.agent.<type>.responses`), builds a Kafka headers map mirroring the JSON headers, sends via ProduceWithValidation, and returns `{AwaitResponse:true, RequestID, ...}`. The engine registers an awaited request and lands the reply in the step's output_field. request_repo_analysis follows this exactly.
- **rag helpers are package-level and reusable as-is:** createRAGEmbeddingClient (ollama, defaults nomic-embed-text + the cluster api_url, overridable via config.embedding_service), applyNomicPrefix (search_query/search_document; only for nomic-* models), pgvectorString, getEmbeddingModel, resolveRAGConfigField, nullIfEmpty, truncateForLog. vectorSearchKB/trigramSearchKB/scanKBResults HARDCODE knowledge_base → wrote code_symbols equivalents.
- **code_symbols upsert/prune pattern:** identity upsert ON CONFLICT(repo,path,symbol) DO UPDATE; keep existing embedding via `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.embedding, code_symbols.embedding)` so unchanged symbols aren't re-embedded; embed only when stored content_hash != new (load existing hashes first); prune `WHERE repo=$1 AND commit_sha IS DISTINCT FROM $current` (skip + log when no commit). content = kind+symbol+signature+doc+path (embedded AND trigram-matched). Method symbols carry the receiver.
- **agent_definitions real shape (from 3 live rows):** columns incl category (freeform: code-driven/orchestrator/specialist) AND agent_category (CHECK: strategist/executor/analyst/integrator/coordinator/specialist, often empty); image_repository 'docker.io/aqls/agent-chassis' tag 'v1.0.1059'; topics `{error,process,response}` templated `{type}`; health_config port 8080 /health /ready; default_config = {workflow{start_step,steps}, processing_mode:"orchestrator", timeout_seconds}; input_contract {required,optional,expects}; output_contract {produces}. code-indexer modelled on these (category code-driven, agent_category integrator). CHECK schema (\d) before applying.
- **Two run-time confirmations for the consumer side:** (1) \d agent_definitions before the INSERT; (2) the collected_data shape of the awaited adapter reply (index_code_symbols reads repo_analysis.output/.commit_sha/.repo; ExtractNestedField tolerates a .response wrapper) — confirm from the first run and adjust configs.
- **Adapter audited against FOCUS_adapter_design (2026-06-11). Conforms:** topic Convention A (system.adapter.analyser.requests + analyser.adapter.group + REQUESTS_TOPIC/CONSUMER_GROUP overrides); ProduceWithValidation arg order (headers before key); sequential handleMessage (no goroutine); NewAdapter manual cleanup on failure; credentials from env not config; in_response_to_request_id from incoming; adapter is the correct pattern (one external system=GitHub, multiple callers, credential boundary).
- **Adapter audit — DIVERGES (fix):** (1) HIGH — envelope: the doc + webscrape + the doc's smoke test put `action` and `reply_to_topic` in the BODY and ids in the Kafka MESSAGE headers (kafka.HeadersToMap(msg.Headers)); my adapter reads action/reply_to_topic from the JSON envelope's typed headers and my sender writes them there. - **Adapter audit — DOC CONTRADICTION (FOCUS_adapter_design vs 003_contracts_and_standards), needs the user to resolve:** (A) body header bool type — 003: typed struct, REAL bools (string bools fail the chassis unmarshal, verified thunder fault); FOCUS skeleton: map[string]string, STRING bools. (B) send call — 003: ProduceWithValidation (never Produce); FOCUS skeleton: Produce. (C) correlation — 003: reuse incoming request_id in response request_id (matcher on request_id); FOCUS: response request_id = NEW uuid + in_response_to_request_id = incoming (matcher on in_response_to_request_id); FOCUS's own smoke test asserts in_response_to_request_id==request's id (supports FOCUS). - **Recommended reconciliation (pending user):** in_response_to_request_id=incoming (both agree); ProduceWithValidation (strict superset; validates real responses, still sends error responses); REAL bools in body but as a map[string]interface{} so it ALSO carries request_id/in_response_to_request_id (canonical types.ResponseHeaders has NEITHER field — the recurring root cause). Open question to user: does the chassis match the awaited row on request_id (003) or in_response_to_request_id (FOCUS)? If in_response_to_request_id → response request_id=fresh uuid; if request_id → keep reused; if unsure → set both to incoming (can't miss either matcher). Also confirm the response body payload field name (FOCUS/git "data" vs canonical types.ResponseBody "body").
- **Meta-finding:** the canonical orchestration/types, git's local mirror, 003, and FOCUS have drifted; the adapter RESPONSE envelope is the area of maximum drift. The user should pick ONE canonical response-envelope spec and align the docs + the validator (FOCUS's own "TODO — tighten validator coverage" notes Tier-2 fields incl in_response_to_request_id aren't validated → silent hangs).
- **003-vs-FOCUS contradiction RESOLVED empirically (2026-06-11) from coordinator.go + git/thunder/dynamic/websearch adapters.** Bools: REAL bools — orchestrator consumes typed types.ResponseMessage; thunder comment (~L634-643) records the string-bool map fails the unmarshal into IsComplete bool; git/thunder/dynamic all typed. websearch is the lone outlier (string-bool map + plain Produce) = the deprecated path the FOCUS skeleton describes. ProduceWithValidation: git/thunder/dynamic use it; only websearch uses Produce; user confirms it's the better validator. request_id: coordinator.go ProcessResponse (L192-197) claims the awaited request on execCtx.InResponseTo.RequestID (=in_response_to_request_id) FIRST, falling back to execCtx.RequestID only if empty → in_response_to_request_id is the load-bearing matcher; a fresh request_id is fine. git's concrete choice: reuse request_id from incoming + add fresh message_id + set in_response_to_request_id (covers both match paths). My adapter's buildResponseKafkaHeaders already does exactly this → response side was already correct.
- **Request-envelope finding (REVISES the prior audit): action is read from the BODY by ALL adapters** (thunder body["action"], git req.Body.Action, image-generator req.Body.Data) — my adapter read headers.action; FIXED. Reply topic is genuinely MIXED: git+websearch read headers (responses_topic/reply_to_topic), thunder+image-generator read body.reply_to_topic — support both (my responses_topic-from-headers was already right; the FOCUS skeleton's body.reply_to_topic was the outlier, NOT my adapter as the prior audit implied). Payload nests under body.data.
- **APPLIED (2026-06-11):** adapter.go — incoming.Body changed from json.RawMessage to a typed struct {Action, Data json.RawMessage, ReplyToTopic}; dispatch on in.Body.Action; unmarshal in.Body.Data; reply topic = headers.ResponsesTopic||headers.ReplyToTopic||body.ReplyToTopic; header comment rewritten to the empirically-grounded contract. analyser_request_action.go (sender) — body now {action, reply_to_topic, data:{owner,repo,ref,language}}; headers keep responses_topic+reply_to_topic+action (belt-and-braces); comments fixed. ## Doc restructure: adapter docs + 003 (thinking + plan, 2026-06-11)

**Diagnosis (precise, after reading 003 §832-890 + coordinator.go).** The "003 vs FOCUS contradiction" is NOT 003 being wrong. 003 already has a dedicated "Adapter Response Envelope Contract" (§832) that is correct on the two things FOCUS's skeleton got wrong: it MANDATES the typed-struct/real-bool pattern (§867-880, the bool trap, citing the 2026-05-22 thunder fault) and ProduceWithValidation (§852/863/888), and it documents the deprecated anti-pattern (§882, which is exactly what FOCUS's skeleton showed). So the contradiction = FOCUS_adapter_design DUPLICATED the envelope in a code skeleton that used the deprecated map/string-bool/Produce path 003 warns against. Root cause is DUPLICATION of normative content that then drifted, not a genuine disagreement of intent.

**The one real 003 imprecision (needs clarification).** 003 §843/856 says "the router matches request_id" and "reuse the incoming request_id in BOTH request_id and in_response_to_request_id; a fresh request_id misses the lookup." coordinator.go ProcessResponse (L192-197) actually claims on execCtx.InResponseTo.RequestID (= in_response_to_request_id) FIRST, falling back to execCtx.RequestID (= request_id) only if empty. So the load-bearing field is in_response_to_request_id, NOT request_id. 003's RECOMMENDED pattern (reuse request_id in both) still WORKS — it sets in_response_to_request_id=incoming (the real key) and request_id=incoming (the fallback) = belt-and-braces. But its MECHANISM wording over-constrains: a fresh request_id is in fact acceptable (the user's instinct), because the match is on in_response_to_request_id. This also harmonises 003 and FOCUS: FOCUS had the mechanism right (match on in_response_to_request_id, request_id=new) but its skeleton used the deprecated bools/Produce; 003 has the safe pattern (reuse request_id, git-style) but mis-describes the mechanism.

**Doc taxonomy (theirs).** Numbered docs = canonical/permanent (001 dev guide, 002 architecture, 003 contracts, 019 tool_library, 020 tool_lifecycle). FOCUS_* = focused design/investigation notes (often transient). Adapters are a first-class component type like tools → they deserve a NUMBERED guide, not a FOCUS_ note. "We need an adapter doc rather than a focus doc" = promote, don't fold.

**Recommendation.**
1. KEEP 003 as the single source for the response-envelope CONTRACT. Apply a SMALL clarification (~15 lines), do NOT expand it with adapter how-to:
   - Correct the matcher wording: the coordinator claims on in_response_to_request_id FIRST (coordinator.go ProcessResponse), request_id is the fallback. The strictly-required rule is in_response_to_request_id = incoming request_id. request_id MAY be a fresh UUID; the favoured pattern (git) reuses the incoming request_id AND adds a fresh message_id, covering both the primary and fallback match — recommend that for new adapters. Drop the "a fresh request_id misses the lookup" claim (true only if in_response_to_request_id is also wrong/absent).
   - Add a short REQUEST-envelope note (currently 003's section is response-only): adapters read action from body.action (NOT headers) — all working adapters do; reply topic is accepted from headers (responses_topic / reply_to_topic) OR body (reply_to_topic) (mixed across adapters); payload at body.data.
   - Add "last verified against code: 2026-06-11 (coordinator.go, git/thunder/dynamic/websearch)" + "if docs and code disagree, code wins."
2. PROMOTE the adapter CONSTRUCTION material to a NUMBERED canonical doc — e.g. 021_adapter_guide.md (sits beside 019_tool_library / 020_tool_lifecycle). Carry over from FOCUS: decision (adapter vs agent vs inline), responsibilities, file/package layout, the struct, NewAdapter cleanup ordering, Run loop (sequential default), graceful Shutdown (sync.Once), health endpoints, topic conventions (A), config YAML field names, deployment/kustomize, credentials/secrets, end-to-end test, pre-merge checklist, common mistakes. For the envelope, LINK to 003 §Adapter Response Envelope Contract and show ONLY the skeleton helper that IMPLEMENTS it — FIXED to typed struct + real bools + ProduceWithValidation (so the skeleton stops contradicting 003), ideally lifted from git-adapter (the reference impl 003 names). Retire FOCUS_adapter_design.
3. Do NOT fold the recipe into 003: it mixes "what must be true" (contract) with "how to build this component" (recipe) and worsens 003's length. The cure for the contradiction is single-sourcing + linking, not merging.
4. 003-too-long is a SEPARATE axis. If slimming: split 003 by contract DOMAIN into numbered sub-docs (message/response-envelope contract; DB+SQL parameterisation; component/theme contracts; agent-definition contract). The response-envelope contract is the prime candidate to extract into its own short numbered doc that BOTH 003 and 021 reference. Optional/later; not needed for this fix.

**Durable anti-drift fix (the meta-point).** The contradiction recurred because a contract lived as PROSE in two places. Promote it to CODE: tighten platform/validation ValidateOutgoingMessage to enforce the Tier-2 routing fields (esp. in_response_to_request_id, message_type, status) when message_type=="response", with the is_error=true escape hatch (this is FOCUS's own "TODO — tighten validator coverage"). An enforced contract can't silently rot into a 30-minute hang, and the doc skeleton can't drift from a validator that rejects the deprecated shape. This is the strongest fix and should be filed as a tracked task.

**Open decisions for the user:** (a) the number for the adapter guide (021_adapter_guide.md?); (b) whether to extract the response-envelope contract into its own numbered doc now or keep it as a 003 section; (c) whether to slim 003 by domain (separate, larger effort). Execution order once decided: apply the small 003 clarification → draft the numbered adapter guide from FOCUS (envelope as a link, skeleton fixed) → retire FOCUS_adapter_design → file the validator-tightening task.

### The diagnosis loop — the conversation's main build (DESIGN + ENGINE + CHASSIS DESIGN done)

## 2026-06-17: diagnosis loop — design updated with the B4a finding + the deterministic SCAFFOLD built & tested
- DESIGN updated (DESIGN_diagnosis_loop.md §1a NEW): the B4a result is now load-bearing in the design. Because symptom retrieval has a CEILING for infrastructure causes (all-methods 0.00 on resultspec), the loop CANNOT re-scope by re-querying the symptom — it must RE-SCOPE BY FOLLOWING THE DATA: runtime evidence is a first-class re-scope driver (the error_log/work-item trace names the layer the symptom can't), and re-scope = the CALL-GRAPH NEIGHBOURHOOD of the evidence-named site (analyser records `calls`), walking toward the cause. Retrieval seeds the FIRST scope; runtime steers every re-scope. This is why the loop beats one-shot retrieval — B4a's own conclusion, now built into the mechanism.
- BUILT the deterministic SCAFFOLD: contextkit/internal/diagnose/loop.go. Boundary kept explicit: the SCAFFOLD (loop control, guards, evidence trail, re-scope) is here and testable WITHOUT a model; the LLM cite-or-abstain VERDICT is an INTERFACE (Verdicter), stubbed in tests, real model on the chassis. Gatherer interface wraps cmd/bundle (read-only); CallGraph interface wraps the analyser `calls` for following. NON-NEGOTIABLE boundaries coded in: gather-only + propose-only, never fix, never trigger; terminal output is a Result (diagnosis + full evidence Trail) for a human.
- GUARDS implemented + each one TESTED (the safety mechanism, so behaviour-tested not eyeballed): iteration-cap, scope-not-narrowing (next scope can't balloon > prev+2), evidence-not-growing (a verdict adding no new citation halts the spin), hypothesis-thrash (oscillation w/o new discriminating evidence). PLUS the item-24 machine rule: a CONFIRMED/REFUTED with NO citation is COERCED to UNVERIFIABLE (a verdict can't stand without grounding). 7 tests, all pass: happy-path confirm, refute-then-confirm-following-call-graph, no-citation coercion, iteration cap, evidence-not-growing, scope-not-narrowing, thrash. go vet clean, whole module builds.
- WHAT'S NOT built (honest): the real Verdicter (the LLM call) — needs the chassis + a model, can't be built/tested here. And the loop has NOT been run against a real known bug yet. The scaffold being correct ≠ the loop diagnosing well; that gate (run it on the gamesdesign bug + 016 §9 catalogue, reproduce the mid-course reversals) still stands before trusting it.
- NEXT options: (a) write the real Gatherer (shell out to cmd/bundle) + CallGraph (read analyser `calls`) adapters — buildable here, testable in part; (b) draft the Verdicter prompt (the §2 contract as an actual prompt template) for the chassis; (c) a cmd/diagnose entrypoint wiring it together. (a) and (c) are concrete next; (b) is the model-side piece.

## 2026-06-17: diagnosis loop — chassis integration design outlined (DESIGN_diagnosis_loop_chassis_integration.md)
- Grounded in the real registry.go: chassis pattern = GlobalActionRegistry (action-name -> ActionDefinition{Handler, Category}); agents are workflows of steps calling registered actions; LLM calls go through the EXISTING execute_llm_prompt action (output_format json) — same one the content-writer uses. Categories include analysis/code; adding "diagnose".
- KEY DECISIONS for the chassis form:
  - The loop is an AGENT (workflow of steps), NOT a new runtime or a CLI — the chassis already provides what it needs (Kafka topics for trigger/result, execute_llm_prompt for the verdict w/ credit+timeout handling, DB access for the gather, spawn/await). A production CLI would duplicate the chassis. cmd/diagnose stays as the DEV/TEST harness only (scripted verdicts, dry-bundle), not production.
  - VERDICT STEP REUSES execute_llm_prompt (the verdict prompt + json output) — NOT a new action. Its JSON output is the wire format verdict_wire.go already parses. (reuse-before-recreate.)
  - LOOP stays in the tested Go engine: prefer a single diagnose_run action wrapping pkg/diagnose.Run with the verdict injected as an execute_llm_prompt call, rather than re-expressing the convergence guards as workflow conditionals/SQL (keep complexity in Go, workflows thin — the standing guidance).
  - GATHERER is the one piece that changes shape: standalone shells out to cmd/bundle (subprocess); chassis must NOT shell out — replace BundleGatherer with a ChassisGatherer implementing the SAME Gatherer interface via in-process read-only actions (analyser read + \d/SELECT/log reads + assemble). Engine unchanged (knows only the interface); the main porting task, isolated behind the interface.
- FILE SPLIT (the user's question): CHASSIS (runs in prod) = pkg/diagnose/ engine+tests (already copied there), the verdict prompt (as an agent_definitions row), the thin new actions (platform/orchestration/actions/, Category "diagnose"), the agent definition workflow (migration). STANDALONE (dev/test only) = cmd/diagnose/main.go (harness), groundtruth_targets.json + B4a artefacts (lex/sem/chassis/embeddings json), the runbooks/design docs.
- TRIGGERING: (a) on-demand by human/agent via a Kafka request {symptom, seed_scope, runtime_site} — START HERE, no new triggering code, person asks + person reads; (b) on build/rebuild failure via existing work-item/error-log machinery — enqueue a diagnose request on failure or complete-but-no-op (the gamesdesign symptom); (c) proactive scheduled sweep — only after the loop is proven on known bugs, still report-only. All three are just a Kafka message; difference is who sends it.
- BUILD ORDER (chassis): port gatherer (ChassisGatherer) -> wrap engine as diagnose_run + diagnose_emit actions, register them, verdict=execute_llm_prompt -> seed agent definition (workflow + prompt) as a migration -> wire trigger (a), test with a known symptom -> the real-bug eval gate (gamesdesign + 016 §9, must reproduce the REVERSALS + abstain when unsettled) before (b)/(c).
- READ-ONLY/HUMAN-GATED boundaries DO NOT relax in the chassis: gather read-only, verdict only judges+cites, loop emits diagnosis+trail for a human. Chassis adds plumbing, not authority. A diagnose agent that could change code/trigger a rebuild is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE.
- The complete-step uses result_from (the singular flatten) — the very contract whose OLD mishandling caused the gamesdesign bug this loop diagnoses; the fixed resolveResultSpec makes result_from correct, so the diagnose agent uses the fixed contract.

This is the shape diagnose-agent's verdict step uses and what diagnose_run parses.

LESSON (added to the cross-module seam lesson): a cross-module copy can be incomplete in TWO ways — a wrong import path on a copied file, AND a file omitted entirely. DESIGN (pure-decision + IO-adapter split, mirroring DecideStep/Run):
- NEW internal/diagnose/docselect.go: DocRule{Doc, Keywords, PathGlobs, Always} + SelectDocs(hypothesis, scope, rules) []string (pure, deterministic, testable) + LoadDocCatalogue(path) ([]DocRule, error). ## 2026-06-17 (cont.): adaptive DB-evidence gather — design + the selection foundation (from the vonc.com handoff transcript)
The vonc.com chat (no loop tooling) did a long MANUAL investigation the loop should automate: ad-hoc SELECTs against DOMAIN tables (pages, page_components, content_components, site_specs, agent_definitions), iteratively NARROWED by each finding (pages -> page_components -> content_components -> history), plus repeated schema-guess + query-rewrite churn. The loop today gathers a FIXED runtime shape (diagnose_load_runtime / dbcontext: agent_error_log + site_work_items + orchestration_states, fixed columns). GAP: the loop follows CODE evidence (call graph) but can't follow DATA evidence (issue a new query against a different table per the verdict).

REUSE FACT (checked dbcontext): dbcontext ALREADY has a `-rows "SELECT ..."` mode with multipass sizing (probe LIMIT N+1, cap, sample) and a no-shell -c exec path. So the EXECUTION primitive for arbitrary read-only SELECTs exists. What's missing is the loop DRIVING it adaptively (which query, bound to the loop's site/page context).

SAFETY BOUNDARY (the load-bearing decision): the model must NOT emit raw SQL. dbcontext -rows runs whatever it's handed, so model-written SQL would break the loop's read-only-by-construction guarantee (expensive query, wrong DB, non-SELECT). DESIGN = a VETTED QUERY CATALOGUE: hand-written, parameterised, \d-verified SELECTs; the loop SELECTS among them by hypothesis (the data analogue of the doc catalogue). The model picks from a menu, never writes SQL. Bonus: this kills the transcript's schema-guess + query-rewrite churn — a catalogue query is \d-verified once, then reused.

THREE LAYERS (only layer 1 new this turn):
- LAYER 1 (BUILT, pure, tested): internal/diagnose/queryselect.go — QueryRule{Name, Title, SQL, Params, Keywords, PathGlobs, Always} + SelectQueries(hypothesis, scope, catalogue) []QueryRule + LoadQueryCatalogue. Matching is IDENTICAL to SelectDocs; extracted shared helpers lower()/scopePaths() into docselect.go so both selectors use one implementation (reuse). 4 tests (keyword+always, path-glob, dedup-by-name, nil) green; docselect tests still pass after the extraction. Params bind to the loop's EXISTING context (site_id, domain, page, correlation_id) — so NO wire-format change and NO model-supplied params in v1.
- LAYER 2 (NEXT, not built): EXECUTION wiring. The gatherer (standalone) / diagnose_load_runtime (chassis) calls SelectQueries(hypothesis, scope, catalogue), binds each query's Params from the loop context, runs it READ-ONLY via dbcontext -rows (standalone) or params.DB QueryContext (chassis), and appends the results to the bundle's runtime section. Standalone: gatherer gains QueryCatalogue []QueryRule + cmd/diagnose a -query-catalogue flag, and per iteration runs `dbcontext -rows <sql>` for each selected query (multipass sizing already caps output). Chassis: diagnose_load_runtime gains a catalogue config + runs the selected queries with its existing params.DB pattern. dbcontext -rows is the reuse; no new executor.
- LAYER 3 (LATER, more powerful, not built): let the VERDICT name a catalogue query + params for targeted drill-down ("page_components_for_page where page_name=index") — the data analogue of the verdict naming next_scope. Needs a wire field (e.g. data_requests: [{query, params}]) + param validation against the catalogue (still NOT raw SQL). The query NAMES + their param lists must be in the bundle/prompt so the model picks from the menu.

STARTER CATALOGUE: contextkit/docs/diagnose_query_catalogue.example.json — 5 queries built ONLY from transcript queries that DEMONSTRABLY RAN (observed columns, not guessed): pages_for_site, page_components_for_page (JOIN content_components ON cc.id=pc.component_id — validated, returned 6 rows), work_items_recent, needs_page_items (spec->>'page_name' — validated), site_specs_current. ## 2026-06-17 (cont.): DB-evidence design revised — model-written SQL under a read-only substrate (NOT a string filter), catalogue demoted to fast-path/examples
User pushed back on the vetted-catalogue-only stance: a hardcoded SELECT list is too limited for open-ended diagnosis (the vonc.com transcript proved it — needed JOINs/drill-downs that couldn't be pre-listed), and proposed "filter the LLM result to just SELECT queries" + a schema-confirm step. ASSESSMENT:
- DIRECTION RIGHT: model-WRITTEN SQL is the better GENERAL mechanism (handles the long tail a catalogue can't; what a human debugger does). Catalogue can't anticipate every shape.
- MECHANISM CORRECTED: "filter to SELECT" by STRING INSPECTION cannot be made safe, and the failure mode is DATA LOSS. Bypasses a prefix check: statement stacking (psql -c runs "SELECT 1; DELETE..."), data-modifying CTEs (WITH t AS (DELETE ... RETURNING *) SELECT...), COPY ... TO PROGRAM (shell exec), side-effecting functions (SELECT pg_terminate_backend(...)). Parsing SQL to reject all of these is intractable.
- RESOLUTION (the design change): safety must be the EXECUTION SUBSTRATE enforcing read-only, not SQL parsing.
  * CHASSIS (diagnose_load_runtime, params.DB): db.BeginTx(ctx, &sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly:true}) + QueryContext(modelSQL). Engine rejects ANY write incl. data-modifying CTEs; pgx extended protocol rejects multi-statement. Driver-enforced, no parsing. + SET LOCAL statement_timeout.
  * HARNESS (dbcontext shells psql): point -psql at a READ-ONLY ROLE (default_transaction_read_only, SELECT-only grants) — stacking moot, nothing can write. + statement_timeout on the role.
- SCHEMA-CONFIRM STEP (user asked for it; primitive already exists): dbcontext has a -schema <tables> mode = \d. Flow: gather schema digest (dbcontext -schema) into the bundle -> model writes SQL against CONFIRMED columns -> execute read-only. Reuses existing tooling; it's schema-before-SQL applied by the model.
- CATALOGUE ROLE SHIFT (queryselect.go + the example catalogue from last turn): NOT the only path now — it's (a) the fast-path for common queries and (b) FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES that show the model real table/column names (cuts schema round-trips). SelectQueries still useful for the common set.
- REJECTED: SQL-string-filter as the safety boundary (the user's literal proposal, mechanism only — the intent is right). Also still rejected: model raw SQL on a READ-WRITE connection.

BUILT THIS TURN (pure, tested, defense-in-depth ONLY): internal/diagnose/sqlguard.go — IsReadOnlySQL(sql) error. A cheap PRE-FLIGHT LINT, explicitly NOT the safety boundary (blunt doc comment + tests): rejects empty, non-SELECT/WITH start, internal ';' (stacking), and write/DDL/privilege/side-effect tokens (insert/update/delete/merge/truncate/drop/alter/create/grant/revoke/copy/call/do/vacuum/analyze/reindex/refresh/cluster/lock/comment/security) on WORD BOUNDARIES (so created_at/updated_at/build_status/claimed_at/deleted don't false-trip — tested). Catches the data-modifying CTE via the delete/update token, and COPY TO PROGRAM via copy. It is DEFENCE IN DEPTH behind the read-only transaction/role — never run model SQL on a read-write connection on the lint alone. 2 tests (accepts/rejects) green. Copied to cmd_diagnose_current/.

REVISED LAYERS:
- Layer 1 (built earlier): SelectDocs/SelectQueries + catalogues (fast-path + examples).
- Layer 2 (NEXT, the real value, needs the substrate): the verdict EMITS a SQL string (a data_request); the loop LINTS it (IsReadOnlySQL) then RUNS it READ-ONLY (chassis BeginTx ReadOnly / harness read-only role) + statement_timeout, with the schema digest (dbcontext -schema) in the bundle so the model writes correct SQL. This is the wire-format change (verdict gains an optional sql/data_request field) + the read-only execution wiring.
- The schema digest in the bundle is the "confirm schema" step.

MUST CONFIRM before wiring Layer 2 execution (schema-before-SQL applied to the SAFETY SUBSTRATE — do NOT assume): (1) does params.DB in the chassis support BeginTx with sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly:true} as wired (it should via database/sql+pgx) AND is there a read-only DB ROLE/DSN available, or do we create one; (2) for the harness, provision a read-only role for -psql (or have dbcontext open its own read-only Go connection instead of shelling psql, to get BeginTx ReadOnly there too); (3) set statement_timeout. These are env/DB-provisioning decisions I can't verify from here.
PENDING: confirm the read-only substrate (above) -> wire Layer 2 (verdict sql field + lint + read-only exec + schema digest in bundle). Then the standing spine (analyser path verification; readSymbolBody; verdict prompt; 5 mechanics; migration; eval gate).

## 2026-06-17 (cont.): three-guard model-SQL — Guards 1+2 BUILT (prompt + parse-lint), Guard 3 (read-only exec) still gated
User confirmed defence-in-depth: (1) prompt says SELECT-only, (2) lint/filter the response, (3) read-only transaction. Roles + order (the failure mode is treating 1/2 as the guarantee): Guard 1 reduces bad-query RATE + makes intent auditable (weakest); Guard 2 = fast, legible rejection before the DB + audit point (string inspection, not complete); Guard 3 = the engine-enforced GUARANTEE (holds if 1+2 fail). NON-NEGOTIABLE: never run model SQL on a read-write connection on the strength of 1+2. Flow: verdict EMITS a data request (Guard 1 shapes) -> loop LINTS on parse (Guard 2) -> gather RUNS read-only (Guard 3).

BUILT THIS TURN (pure, tested; independent of the DB substrate):
- WIRE: Verdict (loop.go) + VerdictWire (verdict_wire.go) gained DataRequests []DataRequest{SQL,Why} — the DATA analogue of NextScope (NextScope = code to gather next; DataRequests = read-only SQL to gather next). One all-strings DataRequest type serves both domain + wire (no enum, so no wire variant needed). ADDITIVE — no existing field renamed (per the don't-rename rule; flagged: new field DataRequests on both structs, new type DataRequest, new VerdictWire json key "data_requests").
- GUARD 2 INTEGRATION: toVerdict now lints each w.DataRequests via IsReadOnlySQL; keeps read-only ones, DROPS the rest, surfacing the reason in NeededEvidence (so the drop is in the trail, not silent) — same fail-safe pattern as the unknown-outcome coercion. So an unsafe request is removed at PARSE, before it can reach execution.
- TEST: TestParseVerdict_DataRequestsLintedAtParse — a verdict with a valid SELECT + a data-modifying CTE + a stacked statement parses to ONLY the SELECT, with "dropped non-read-only data_request" in NeededEvidence. Green. (Fixed: verdict_wire_test.go needed the strings import.)
- GUARD 1 (prompt): PROMPT_diagnosis_verdict.md — added data_requests to the output schema (kept in lockstep with verdict_wire.go as the doc itself requires) + a new hard rule 7: data_requests are READ-ONLY SELECT/WITH only, against the bundle's schema, no writes/DDL/COPY/CALL/multi-statement (else rejected + dropped → wastes an iteration), they run read-only so don't try to change anything, ask the narrowest read, name tables/columns from the bundle's schema section.

## 2026-06-17 (cont.): confirming the read-only connection (Guard 3) — both sides + runbook §4d
How to confirm Guard 3 on each side (the prerequisite before any data_request executes; failure mode = data loss, so confirm not assume):
- CHASSIS (diagnose_load_runtime via params.DB): params.DB is a *sql.DB (dev guide shows WriteSiteSpec(ctx, db *sql.DB,…) + maintenance actions use params.DB.QueryContext), so BeginTx(ctx,&sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly:true}) is available with NO new connection. Pattern: BeginTx ReadOnly -> defer Rollback (never commit) -> SET LOCAL statement_timeout -> QueryContext(modelSQL). Engine rejects writes incl. data-modifying CTEs; pgx extended protocol rejects multi-statement. CONFIRM: (1) params.DB type + DSN — built in buildActionParams() in coordinator.go (dev guide §12); grep ActionParams / BeginTx / buildActionParams. (2) PROVE a read-only tx refuses a write against the live DB: psql -c 'BEGIN READ ONLY;' -c 'DELETE FROM site_work_items WHERE false;' -c 'ROLLBACK;' — expect "cannot execute DELETE in a read-only transaction". WHERE false matches nothing so the probe is non-destructive even on a RW connection. If it does NOT error, read-only isn't taking effect — don't run model SQL. Belt-and-braces: a SELECT-only ROLE DSN; check with \dp + \du.
- HARNESS (cmd/diagnose -> dbcontext -> psql -c): psql -c STACKS statements, so a tx wrapper around model SQL is NOT safe (the model's own ; escapes it). Safe option = a READ-ONLY ROLE in -psql (default_transaction_read_only on, SELECT-only grants, statement_timeout) — stacking moot. CONFIRM via \du; create diagnose_ro if absent (CREATE ROLE … ; GRANT SELECT … ; ALTER ROLE … SET default_transaction_read_only=on); prove with psql as that role: DELETE … WHERE false -> must error. ALTERNATIVE (more code, removes the stacking foot-gun structurally): dbcontext opens its OWN *sql.DB + BeginTx(ReadOnly) like the chassis instead of shelling psql.
- Runbook updated: RUNBOOK_design_diagnosis_loop.md §4d "Confirming the read-only connection (Guard 3)" inserted between §4c (port sequence) and §5 (eval gate) — chassis side, harness side, the non-destructive WHERE-false write-refusal probe, and "what this gates" (only after a side refuses a write do you wire the gather that EXECUTES data_requests + the dbcontext -schema schema-digest gather).
PENDING: run the §4d probes (user-side, needs the cluster/DB) -> confirm read-only on the chosen side -> wire Guard 3 execution + schema-digest gather + the gather that runs surviving data_requests into the next bundle. Then the standing spine (analyser path verification; readSymbolBody; 5 mechanics; migration; eval gate).

## 2026-06-17 (cont.): pgbouncer + the read-only connection (Guard 3) — runbook §4d corrected
User confirmed the BEGIN READ ONLY probe REFUSES a write (DELETE … WHERE false on site_flows -> "cannot execute DELETE in a read-only transaction"), AND that the stack uses pgbouncer. pgbouncer changes the picture by POOL MODE:
- CHASSIS (params.DB.BeginTx(ctx,&sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly:true})): this is the RIGHT mechanism under a pooler because read-only is TRANSACTION-SCOPED and cleaned up by Rollback regardless of which backend the pool hands out. SAFE under transaction pooling (the usual mode): BEGIN..query..ROLLBACK all run on one assigned backend. CONFIRM pool_mode (SHOW CONFIG on the pgbouncer admin db port 6432, or the configmap). transaction -> safe as written; session -> still safe for BeginTx but NEVER a bare session-level SET (leaks to next client); statement -> transactions don't hold (rule out; the probe behaving as a real tx — psql *#/!# state — is evidence it's NOT statement mode).
- HARNESS (psql -c, which STACKS): CORRECTED — was "ALTER ROLE … SET default_transaction_read_only=on", which DOES NOT reliably apply under pgbouncer transaction pooling (pgbouncer reuses backends, doesn't replay per-role startup params per pooled client). Switched to GRANT-BASED enforcement: a role with ONLY SELECT (no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grant) + ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES … GRANT SELECT for future tables; a write then fails on PERMISSIONS ("permission denied for table …") regardless of pooling/tx state. statement_timeout set per-connection in the DSN (?options=-c%20statement_timeout%3D5s), not via ALTER ROLE, same pgbouncer reason. Updated the expected probe error (permission denied, not the read-only-tx message). Kept the dbcontext-opens-own-*sql.DB+BeginTx alternative (clean under transaction pooling, removes both the stacking and the SET problems).
- KEY LESSON: under pgbouncer, TRANSACTION-SCOPED read-only (BeginTx ReadOnly) and GRANT-based read-only are robust; SESSION-level SET (ALTER ROLE SET / SET outside a tx) is NOT — it leaks across pooled clients or silently doesn't apply. The chassis path is already the robust kind; only the harness guidance needed fixing.
- Runbook §4d updated on both sides (chassis pgbouncer note + harness GRANT-based role). NOTES current.
PENDING: confirm pgbouncer pool_mode (expected: transaction) -> chassis BeginTx(ReadOnly) path is then good to wire; for the harness, create the SELECT-only diagnose_ro role (GRANT-based) + DSN statement_timeout. Then wire Guard 3 execution + the dbcontext -schema schema-digest gather + the gather that runs surviving data_requests. Then the standing spine (analyser path verification; readSymbolBody; 5 mechanics; migration; eval gate).

## 2026-06-17 (cont.): chassis Guard 3 CONFIRMED — pgbouncer pool_mode = transaction
The pgbouncer-config configmap shows pool_mode = transaction (each transaction gets one backend, released on completion). Combined with the earlier BEGIN READ ONLY probe refusing a write, the chassis Guard-3 path is CONFIRMED good: params.DB is *sql.DB (types.go upload confirms ActionParams.DB *sql.DB), BeginTx(ctx,&sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly:true}) is transaction-scoped (safe under transaction pooling — cleaned up by Rollback regardless of backend reuse), engine enforces read-only. No code blocker remains on the chassis side for running a linted model SELECT read-only.
Two details from the configmap:
- admin user is pgbouncer_admin (the earlier `-U <admin>` was literal -> "bash: admin: No such file or directory"). Runbook §4d corrected to pgbouncer_admin.

HARNESS side unchanged from the last entry: under transaction pooling, ALTER ROLE … SET default_transaction_read_only is unreliable -> use a GRANT-based SELECT-only role (diagnose_ro) + DSN statement_timeout. (Only needed if running model SQL from the standalone harness; the chassis path is the primary.)
PENDING: chassis Guard 3 confirmed -> wire diagnose_load_runtime to run surviving data_requests under BeginTx(ReadOnly) + SET LOCAL statement_timeout, and add the dbcontext -schema schema-digest gather into the bundle (so the model writes SQL against confirmed columns). Then the standing spine (analyser path verification; readSymbolBody; 5 mechanics; migration; eval gate).

## 2026-06-17 (cont.): schema-digest into the bundle (the confirm-schema INPUT for data_requests) — built + tested

# 006 — News Feed Pipeline

Implementation guide for the content feed pipeline. Covers: architecture, all deployed components, operational procedures, resolved issues, and expansion roadmap.

Test site: gaswholesalers.com (`5fe15466-4e2e-4ff2-981e-98c1b7074002`)

---

## Current Status — Working End-to-End

The pipeline is fully operational for gaswholesalers.com with homepage news snippets AND a dedicated news listing page, both driven entirely by the automated pipeline.

| Layer | Status | Evidence |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Source seeding | ✅ Deployed | `SeedContentSourcesAction` reads classification spec, creates `content_sources` |
| Ingestion (RSS) | ✅ Working | 5 articles per run from OilPrice |
| Ingestion (news_search) | ✅ Working | 2-5 articles per run via web search adapter |
| Ingestion (api_news/Grok) | ✅ Working | 4-5 articles per run via xAI Responses API with web + X search |
| Ingestion (scrape) | ✅ Working | 20 items per run (nav links — filtered by triage) |
